artifactEvidence.excerpt: On September 10, DeepSeek introduced V4.1-Flash, a new model with native image understanding. That means it can use a picture as part of what it receives, rather than working only from words. Vercel had made the model available through its AI Gateway a day earlier.

A model does the generating behind an app’s interface, and the app maker chooses which model to connect. Picture a photo app: if its maker connects it to V4.1-Flash and passes along the image, the model can consider the picture when it answers. The new ability is underneath; the app’s own update tells you what is available in the tool you use.

explainBack.question: Why might my chat app still ignore the photo I upload, even though DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash with native image understanding two days ago?
explainBack.answer: Because the model is only one layer. Your app's maker decides which model sits behind the interface and whether the app forwards your image to it. If the maker hasn't connected V4.1-Flash, or connects it but never passes the picture along in the request, the model never receives the image — so nothing changes for you regardless of DeepSeek's announcement.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: A correct answer must use the article's causal chain: capability lives in the model (P002), the app maker chooses the connection and must pass the image (P003), and the app's own update is the authoritative signal of what you actually get.
explainBack.assessment: The article supports this answer fully in ordinary language; a reader relying only on P002–P003 can reconstruct every causal step without gaps.

unseenTransfer.scenario: On September 16, a small expense-tracking app that has advertised 'powered by DeepSeek V4-Pro' suddenly behaves differently: replies come faster and read differently, and the developer has shipped no update. A colleague asks whether the app was hacked or silently changed.
unseenTransfer.question: Using only the article's mechanism, what most likely happened, and how could a user check whether the app can now understand photographed receipts?
unseenTransfer.answer: Most likely nothing at the app changed: from September 14, requests sent under the older deepseek-v4-pro label are scheduled to route to V4.1-Flash until V4.1-Pro launches, so the model behind the unchanged interface was swapped upstream. Whether receipts-as-photos now work is a separate question — the app must accept an image and pass it to the model; the user should check whether the app offers image upload and what its own release notes claim, rather than assuming the routing switch added a visible feature.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: Applies P004's label routing to explain the silent behaviour change and P003's connect-and-pass-along mechanism to separate upstream capability from app-level availability.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism resolves this novel scenario completely; both the routing note and the interface/model layering carry over without new assumptions, confirming genuine transfer.
